title: Stubnerkogel Suspension Bridge & Viewing Platform
name: Stubnerkogel Suspension Bridge & Viewing Platform
kurzbeschreibung: The 140 m long suspension bridge on the Stubnerkogel at 2,200 m above sea level: airy panoramic views, the Glocknerblick viewing platform, and the Felsenweg in the high mountains.
beschreibung:
Overview

The spectacular Stubnerkogel Hängebrücke swings at an altitude of 2,200 metres right next to the mountain station of the Stubnerkogelbahn across a deep rocky abyss in the Goldberggruppe of the Hohe Tauern. With a total length of around 140 metres and a width of barely one metre, this daring structure was the first year-round accessible suspension bridge at this altitude in Europe. The popular excursion destination combines breathtaking drops with an overwhelming 360-degree high-alpine panorama of the Großglockner, the Gasteinertal, and the glaciated peaks of the Hohe Tauern.

Route & Requirements

The bold suspension bridge was designed as an ethereal, transparent cable-stayed construction: the walkway consists of galvanized grating and wire-mesh railings, allowing visitors to peer straight into the roughly 30-metre-deep abyss beneath their feet. Engineered to withstand wind speeds of up to 200 km/h, the bridge delivers a thrilling rush of adrenaline for sure-footed adventurers free from vertigo. Directly opposite the bridge, a short scenic trail leads to the circular viewing platform Glocknerblick: this futuristic steel-and-glass construction cantilevers out over the cliff edge and, on clear days, opens up direct views of Austria's highest peak, the Großglockner (3,798 m). Another highlight is the roughly 100-metre-long Felsenweg: a secured steel walkway clings to steep rock faces leading out to a dramatic viewing platform overlooking the Gasteinertal.

Visit & Arrival

The Stubnerkogelbahn and the suspension bridge are open daily from 08:30 to 16:00 during the summer season from early June to mid-October as well as during the ski season. Walking across the suspension bridge and accessing all viewing platforms is free with a cable car ticket. Summer lift fares (season 2025/2026): round trip adults approx. €36.00, children (born 2009–2018) approx. €18.00. Holders of regional guest cards receive discounts. Getting there by public transport: ÖBB (Tauernbahn) directly to Bad Gastein railway station; the valley station of the Stubnerkogelbahn is located right next to the station exit and can be reached in just two minutes on foot. By car: via the B167 (Gasteiner Bundesstraße) to Bad Gastein; car parks are available at the valley station.

Tips

Access from the mountain station to the suspension bridge and the mountain inn is level and barrier-free for visitors; the suspension bridge itself sways gently in the wind and requires a good head for heights. Stop by the modern Bergrestaurant Stubnerkogel and savour hearty alpine snacks on the large panoramic terrace.
